topic: Polynomial-time Poisson phase retrieval with a Parseval-completed iid Gaussian block POVM
overall_status: Primary high-probability convex estimator theorem identified; exact Poissonized POVM reduction proved; fixed-N guarantee follows by conditioning with an explicit sqrt(N) tail penalty; polar-normalized correlated-frame theorem remains unknown.

claims.statement: For iid complex isotropic sub-Gaussian sensing rows satisfying E phi=E phi^2=0, E|phi|^2=1, E|phi|^4=1+mu>1, and conditionally independent observations Y_j~Pois(|<phi_j,w>|^2), Huang-Li-Needell Theorem 1 states that when m>=L d a convex PSD least-squares estimator followed by top-eigenvector extraction obeys dist(z_*,w)<=C3 max{K,1/||w||} sqrt(d/m), with probability 1-O(exp(-c d)); the source says the guarantee holds simultaneously for all signals. For standard complex Gaussian entries mu=1. L,c,C3 are hidden constants depending on K,mu.
assumptions: Rows have independent entries and are independent across j.
No additive background, saturation, or unmodeled detector noise.
CVX-LS is the global solution of the convex PSD least-squares program; numerical solver precision is an additional implementation issue.
claims.status: Source-reported primary theorem checked against arXiv v1 Theorem 1, Assumptions 1-2, and CVX-LS setup; not independently proof-audited.
claims.novelty_boundary: Published Poisson phase-retrieval result; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: m Poisson rows and their full count data; theorem treats iid row measurements, not a normalized tight frame.
claims.falsifier: Mismatch in the primary theorem assumptions, estimator, rate, probability, or uniformity statement.

claims.statement: On a good singular-value event for iid Gaussian G in C^(m x d), choose a=1/(4m) and R=(I-a G*G)^(1/2). Then Btilde=[sqrt(a)G;R] is Parseval with m+d outputs. With uniform detector efficiency eta_det and Poissonized launch mean N, its first m channel counts are independent Poisson with means N eta_det a |g_j*x|^2=|g_j*w|^2 for deterministic w=sqrt(N eta_det a)x. Thus the iid-row Poisson theorem applies exactly to the Gaussian block; residual and loss/no-click outputs complete the POVM and remain charged in the total launch budget.
assumptions: G has iid standard complex Gaussian entries; m is at least a sufficiently large constant times d.
On the good event lambda_min(G*G)>=m/4 and lambda_max(G*G)<=4m; otherwise a fixed valid fallback POVM is used and this event counts as failure.
x is a unit vector and detector efficiency is uniform and known.
The Poissonized source has expected total N input photons, so all output counts, including residual/no-click, sum to Pois(N).
claims.status: Direct algebraic POVM/count-law reduction plus standard Gaussian singular-value concentration.
claims.novelty_boundary: A measurement-model transfer of a published estimator theorem; this is not the polar-normalized Gaussian Parseval frame.
claims.costs: N launched photons across all m+d output channels and loss/no-click events; m+d=O(d); frame synthesis/calibration remains separately charged.
claims.falsifier: A violation of Parseval completeness, the stated click probability, or the exact Poisson mean identity.

claims.statement: Under the preceding completed-Gaussian-block policy, if N eta_det>=max{4m/K^2,16 C3^2 K^2 d/epsilon^2}, the normalized top-eigenvector CVX-LS estimate has phase error at most epsilon with high probability in the Poissonized experiment. In particular its squared error on the success event is O(d/(N eta_det)); m=Theta(d) gives N eta_det=O(d/epsilon^2) launched-photon scaling with hidden constants.
assumptions: The Huang-Li-Needell source theorem and good-frame event hold.
The estimated signal is normalized to unit norm; the theorem scale is sqrt(N eta_det a).
Ideal exact frame calibration and exact integer counts.
claims.status: Proved reduction from primary theorem; hidden constants and conventional convex-optimization precision caveats retained.
claims.novelty_boundary: Conditional rate transfer only; no hardware energy advantage or minimax-constant claim.
claims.costs: N launched photons; Gaussian-block detection fraction at least eta_det/16 on the good event; all residual/no-click outcomes counted.
claims.falsifier: A flaw in the source CVX-LS theorem, scaling/normalization derivation, or good-frame event.

claims.statement: For exactly N launched photons, the full Parseval POVM output counts are multinomial. The fixed-N law is the all-outcome Pois(N q_i) law conditioned on total count N. For any success event determined by the Gaussian-block counts, its fixed-N failure probability is at most the Poissonized failure probability divided by P(Pois(N)=N), which is O(sqrt(N)) times the Poissonized failure. This yields failure O(sqrt(N) exp(-c d))+P(bad frame), exponentially small for polynomial N in d.
assumptions: All POVM output channels and the no-click/loss category are included in the conditioned total.
The Poissonized success event uses the same estimator and depends only on Gaussian-block counts.
The source failure probability is O(exp(-c d)).
claims.status: Direct conditioning proof; de-Poissonization penalty is explicit and may be loose.
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary Poisson-multinomial conditioning; no new concentration theorem.
claims.costs: Exactly N input photons including all no-click and residual events.
claims.falsifier: A mismatch between the full POVM multinomial law and the conditional independent-Poisson law.

claims.statement: The source theorem permits bounded complex sub-Gaussian entries rather than only Gaussian entries. The distribution P(phi=0)=3/4 and P(phi=2 zeta)=1/16 for each zeta in {1,i,-1,-i} has E phi=E phi^2=0, E|phi|^2=1, E|phi|^4=4 and hence mu=3, so row coefficients can be drawn exactly from {0,+-2,+-2i}.
assumptions: The entries and rows are independent with the stated common distribution.
m/d is large enough for the corresponding sub-Gaussian singular-value bounds and source theorem.
claims.status: Moment calculation proved directly; application of source theorem is conditional on its sub-Gaussian assumptions.
claims.novelty_boundary: An explicit finite-alphabet instance of the published theorem assumptions; no new phase-retrieval theorem.
claims.costs: O(d^2) exact row coefficients plus calibration and synthesis of the residual completion.
claims.falsifier: A moment-calculation error or violation of the theorem assumptions by the stated finite distribution.

unknown: Whether a polynomial-time estimator with this rate is already proved directly for the polar-normalized random Parseval frame B=G(G*G)^(-1/2), whose rows are correlated.
A direct fixed-N multinomial CVX-LS theorem avoiding the O(sqrt(N)) de-Poissonization failure penalty.
Numerical values for the hidden sample ratio L, failure exponent c, and estimator constant C3 in the primary theorem.
Robustness thresholds for finite frame calibration error, residual-completion error, background counts, nonuniform loss, detector quantization, saturation, and approximate SDP solving.
Physical optical network/control energy and calibration-exposure costs for realizing the Parseval completion; no hardware advantage is established.
